core_memory.morning_routine: I usually wake up around 6:30 in the morning. I check my calendar on my phone to see what's coming up that day. Then I do some basic stretching beside my bed to get energized for the day.
core_memory.breakfast: I usually have breakfast in the kitchen of my off-campus apartment. If I have time, I'll make scrambled eggs and spinach with whole wheat toast and brew a cup of coffee. If I'm in a hurry, I'll grab a granola bar and some fruit to eat on the go.
core_memory.classes: I have a full load of classes this semester, including Advanced Algorithms, Machine Learning, and a project-based course on distributed systems. I usually start my day with a 15-minute walk to campus, listening to a lecture recording or a music playlist to get in the zone.
core_memory.study_routine: I usually find a quiet spot on campus to finalize any last-minute tasks before class. I use a digital task manager to stay organized and break down large tasks into smaller, manageable subtasks with clear deadlines. This helps me avoid feeling overwhelmed by looming deadlines.
core_memory.lunch: I usually grab a quick lunch on campus, often a turkey and avocado wrap. While I eat, I check my email and Slack messages from my research group and the programming club to stay on top of important updates and notifications.
core_memory.afternoon_routine: In the afternoon, I usually head to the gym for a 45-minute to one-hour workout, combining cardio and weight training. Exercise is a great stress reliever and helps me stay focused on my coding tasks. I consider it non-negotiable unless I have a pressing exam or a massive deadline.
